public_rationale: On 2026-09-28, Marcus wrote that he agrees with Florida's Attorney General that OpenAI does not have the ability to 'properly' regulate its own technology. This judges whether OpenAI's self-governance is good enough. The claim gives no measure or test for 'properly'. 'Ability' could also mean technical capacity or institutional willingness. A Florida Phoenix report from 2026-09-28 says the AG filed for a temporary injunction that day. It also says the AG claims OpenAI has admitted it cannot regulate its own technology (e1). That is an allegation in a pending case, not a finding. In the same report, OpenAI said that on 2026-09-25 it paused training its most capable models until it has additional safeguards (e2). Help Net Security reported in August 2026 that after the OpenAI-Hugging Face incident, OpenAI paused some frontier model inference in research clusters and later restored a more limited path (e3). These facts can be checked, but they do not decide whether OpenAI's self-regulation is proper. Readers who accept them can still reach opposite conclusions. The claim is therefore recorded as an opinion and is not graded.
limitations: The searches found no court ruling on Florida's injunction motion by the evaluation date. Court records were not checked directly.
No independent audit or regulator finding on OpenAI's internal safety governance was found.
The Axios report on the security incidents could not be read (HTTP 403).
The evidence does not establish the details or cause of the OpenAI-Hugging Face incident.

No plain reading gives a yes-or-no test. So the claim is treated as an opinion and is not graded.
